articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 4
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Steelers-Browns game.

Week 4 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ CAR

Six touchdowns in three games is quite the feat. It's LaDainian Tomlinson stuff (2006).
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs LAC

The league leader in fantasy points seems unstoppable, regardless of matchup.
 3. Josh Allen, QB1 vs NE

He has rushed for two touchdowns in each game. Can the Patriots stop him?
 4. Bijan Robinson, RB2 @ NO

He has scored more than 30 points in two of three games. 
 5. Lamar Jackson, QB2 vs TEN

The 50 rushing yards from the Week 3 win are a terrific sign.
 6. Ja'Marr Chase, WR2 vs JAX

 7. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR3 @ CAR

 8. Puka Nacua, WR4 @ PHI

A hip injury has cost him two games. At least the Rams play at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
 9. Jonathan Taylor, RB3 @ WSH

More than 20 touches each week, which is nice when he doesn't score a TD or two.
 10. Derrick Henry, RB4 vs TEN

You know he always wants to shine against his former Titans teammates. 
 11. Kenneth Walker III, RB5 @ LV

The volume was down a bit, but he scores TDs. Note: Chiefs are on a bye in Week 5. Plan ahead!
 12. Christian McCaffrey, RB6 vs DEN

The 49ers are keeping his volume well in check. It's a tough matchup with the Broncos this week.
 13. Brock Purdy, QB3 vs DEN

 14. Patrick Mahomes, QB4 @ LV

 15. Tyler Shough, QB5 vs ATL

 16. Trevor Lawrence, QB6 @ CIN

His investors could have used the rushing TD he gave to a teammate on Sunday.
 17. Justin Jefferson, WR5 vs MIA

An ankle injury could cost him Week 4. It's too early to panic about the team's QBs.
 18. Chris Olave, WR6 vs ATL

 19. Ashton Jeanty, RB7 vs KC

 20. James Cook III, RB8 vs NE

The argument that his QB steals the rushing TDs doesn't work. Cook is great.
 21. Jalen Hurts, QB7 vs LAR

Mild concern over a disappointing Monday effort. The Rams visit Philly Sunday. That's not great, either.
 22. Joe Burrow, QB8 vs JAX

 23. Bryce Young, QB9 vs DET

 24. Matthew Stafford, QB10 @ PHI

If a third-string QB can light up the Eagles, what do you think Stafford can do?
 25. CeeDee Lamb, WR7 @ HOU

Some may try to fade top Cowboys against the Texans, but that is a mistake. 
 26. Drake London, WR8 @ NO

Any worries about his production ended in Week 3. London dominated the Packers. 
 27. Marcus Mariota, QB11 vs IND

One of the best backups in the business remains a solid investment this week.
 28. Kyler Murray

articles.headline: Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City have confirmed the club have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・C、プレミアリーグ違反問題の有罪判決に対し控訴
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、プレミアリーグの財務違反問題における有罪判決に対し、正式に不服申し立てを行いました。
articles.body:
Manchester City have confirmed the club have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

The decision of the independent commission was published on Tuesday and detailed how City arranged "sham" commercial deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by £900 million ($1.2b billion) during a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The club have branded the verdict "unsafe." City announced their appeal in a statement posted on their official website on Friday.

It read: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday, October 1 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

- Downing Street clarifies Andy Burnham's remarks on Man City case

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case."

The Premier League confirmed that City "lodged the appeal to the Chair of the Judicial Panel" and that "the independent Appeal Board hearing will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted."

Fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions are among "a broad discretion" of sanctions available to the commission, the Premier League also said.

The Appeal Board, appointed by the Chair of the Judicial Panel, "must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office, and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board," their statement on Friday added.

In their previous statement on Tuesday, the Premier League called for any appeal to be "concluded as soon as possible."

Immediately following the publication of the independent commission's findings on Tuesday, City CEO Ferran Soriano sent a video message to staff insisting the club are innocent.

He said: "The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation -- that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true."

Sources have told ESPN that part of City's appeal is expected to claim that the money in question came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

The argument is likely to raise questions about whether City are privately-owned -- which the club has maintained since the takeover in 2008 -- or owned by the state of Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: Trail Blazers fire new announcer over past inappropriate posts
articles.description: The Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.
articles.headlineJa: トレイルブレイザーズ、過去の不適切な投稿を理由に新アナウンサーを解雇
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズは実況アナウンサーとしてブレイデン・ベル氏を採用したものの、彼が10代の頃に行った一連の不適切なSNS投稿が明らかになったため、同日中に解雇しました。
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.

"The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments," the team said in a social media statement Thursday announcing Bell's dismissal. "Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster."

Among the insensitive comments, as found by a reporter for KGW in Portland, were Bell saying he was "not racist" but "Asian people piss me off" and a number of misogynistic posts, including him shouting out "big girls" and "closet whores." The posts were reportedly made in 2012 and 2013, around the time that Bell was 15 years old.

Bell, 29, had been hired to call games after broadcasting for the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury and G League's Valley Suns over the past two years.

Both Bell and his agent did not respond to requests for comment from multiple outlets. The agent referred questions from KGW, made before the firing, to the Trail Blazers.

"We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City," the Trail Blazers said. "We strongly believe that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better."

Bell was set to replace longtime play-by-play announcer Kevin Calabro, who had held the role since 2016 but left in July after what he told The Oregonian was a "subprime" contract offer.

New Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon has made a number of cost-cutting moves that have come under scrutiny. Dundon also insisted over the summer that only public money should be used to pay for a $600 million makeover of the Trail Blazers' arena, the Moda Center.

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups for Week 4: Raymond, Allen, Waller among top options
articles.description: If injuries or tough matchups have you seeking help, Matt Bowen provides options at each key position.
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

Looking at the Week 4 NFL slate -- and the available players -- I'll start with the wide receiver position. I have two veteran pass catchers who are seeing consistent volume and producing solid fantasy numbers. There are options at quarterback, too, and one signal-caller could be getting his top target back. We'll also hit on the running backs in line to see an increased role due to injury, plus I have a tight end and a defense to get into lineups.

Wide receivers

Kalif Raymond, Chicago Bears (48.4% rostered; vs. Jets)

The Bears haven't announced whether Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent will start at QB for the Week 4 home game versus the Jets, but either way I'm still pushing for Raymond based on his route deployment in Ben Johnson's offense. Raymond scored 21 points in the Week 3 win over the Eagles, and he has at least five receptions in all three games played this season. Raymond will see the ball as an outlet on crossers, sit routes and unders, plus he has the speed to create big plays (deep over routes and verticals). Raymond fits as a WR3 this week.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (46.6% rostered; vs. Commanders)

Allen is a fit for a Colts passing game missing its vertical element with Alec Pierce out with a heel injury. Allen can uncover or make himself available to the quarterback, which we saw in the Week 3 game versus Houston. Allen caught six of a season-high nine targets for 63 yards and a score (18.3 points). Allen has six receptions in two of three games played, and he gets a solid matchup in Week 4 against the Commanders. Managers can start Allen as a WR3.

Mack Hollins, New England Patriots (11.2% rostered; at Bills)

The Bills have been zone-heavy under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, and they play from a two-deep safety look on 49.2% of opponent dropbacks. That works for Hollins, as he has the coverage awareness to find open voids on short-to-intermediate throws. Hollins caught six of nine targets for 87 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Jaguars (14.7 points), and he has seen at least five targets in two of three games played. He's a deeper-league option this week.

Malik Washington, Miami Dolphins (23.3% rostered; at Vikings)

You can take a shot on Washington because of his versatility and expanding role. articles.headline: FA: Man City verdict has 'significant implications for integrity of game'
articles.description: The Football Association expressed its concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.
articles.headlineJa: FA：マンチェスター・シティ裁定は「競技の公平性に重大な影響を及ぼす」
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドサッカー協会（FA）は、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反を巡るマンチェスター・シティへの有罪判定が競技の「公平性」を損なうとして懸念を表明しました。
articles.body:
The Football Association expressed its concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.

The FA's full statement read: "The Independent Commission's decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

Friday is the deadline for City to appeal the guilty verdict into their breaches of Premier League rules. They have stated that they intend to appeal.

The commission concluded more than £830 million ($1.1 bn) of such funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial rules through a series of "sham" arrangements.

The 40-page core decision published Tuesday shows the independent commission rejected the CPC explanation as "untrue" in its findings, adding: "We concluded that it was an 'explanation' that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme."

Sponsor Etihad Airways, which is owned by an Abu Dhabi fund chaired by City owner Sheikh Mansour's brother, is considering legal action against the Premier League.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC earlier this week that he would be concerned if City's owners sold the club due to the guilty verdict because they have been "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester." But a No. 10 Downing Street spokesman afterwards: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City

But Jamie Carragher wrote for The Telegraph: "The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up."

Gary Neville insisted the entire league has suffered due to City's guilty verdict, saying on the Stick To Football podcast on Disney+: "To listen to this, it is chilling.

"We always think that we've got an enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard, and that it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match-fixing, referee scandals.
